title: Enterprise Governance Boundary
outOfScope: Configuring or verifying an adopter's identity provider, branch protection, SSO, legal/compliance program, production sandbox, or provider account.
Claiming SOC 2, ISO 27001, SLSA, immutable audit, complete prompt-injection defense, or production readiness from repository-local evidence.
Publishing a release or changing release identity; release publication remains WI-17.

sources.reason: Canonical repository-local versus external enterprise boundary source.
Existing capability truth and enterprise assurance limitation.
Existing governance and overclaim regression coverage.

Adopter-facing checklist distinguishing local evidence from external controls.
Executable status-vocabulary, required-control, and unsupported-claim regression checks.
English product boundary and WI-16 publication gate entry point.

riskAssessment.reason: Enterprise controls are external and adopter-specific; WI-11 can verify only the repository boundary, status vocabulary, and overclaim prevention.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized serial execution; WI-11 is bounded to repository-local enterprise boundary evidence and external-control handoff.

preReviewWarnings: Review every control status, forbidden assurance claim, external-control handoff, and multilingual boundary statement; do not treat fixture or repository evidence as adopter verification.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Repository documentation clearly separates repository-local evidence, SDLC support, and external enterprise controls, and explicitly rejects unsupported SOC 2, ISO 27001, SLSA, identity, immutable-audit, sandbox, complete-injection-defense, and production-readiness claims.

The machine-readable enterprise control matrix uses only external_control_required, configured, verified, not_configured, not_applicable, or unknown and covers identity, authorization, review, branch protection, separation of duties, signed commits/tags, release immutability, least privilege, secrets, audit retention, data classification/transfer, incident response, legal hold, SBOM, provenance, and vulnerability/dependency controls.

Adopter checklist and English/Japanese/Chinese boundary references distinguish repository evidence from adopter-required evidence without claiming external verification; regression tests reject unknown statuses and overclaims.
Focused governance/documentation tests, full quality, required AI checks, and status/document alignment pass.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: AI Cockpit records strong repository-local governance evidence, but adopters could misread those records as enterprise identity, compliance, sandbox, immutable-audit, or production-control verification.
constraints: Use explicit status vocabulary and fail closed on unknown control states.
Keep adopter/provider/legal controls external and do not invent evidence.
Preserve the Japanese gate: WI-11 may align Japanese boundary wording but cannot declare WI-16 capability assessment passed.
Do not publish or mutate release identity in this Work Item.
intent.rationale: A machine-readable boundary and adopter checklist make unsupported enterprise claims difficult to express while preserving useful repository governance evidence.

declaredIntent.summary: Define repository-local versus external enterprise control boundaries and prevent unsupported compliance/security claims.
